title: Income of Other Persons included in Total Income of Assessee
outcomes: Apply provisions on transfer of income and revocable transfers.
Club income of spouse and son's wife.
Club income of a minor child and apply the exemption.
Apply HUF conversion, deemed ownership and recovery provisions.

meta.exam_tip: Name the relationship and the section first, then compute the clubbed share.

concepts.title: Transfers of income and revocable transfers
body: Sections 96 to 100 prevent tax avoidance by diverting income to family members. Section 96: where income is transferred without transferring the asset, the income remains taxable in the transferor's hands, whether the transfer is revocable or not.

Section 97(1): income from a revocable transfer of assets is taxed in the transferor's hands. A transfer is revocable if it contains a provision for re-transfer of the income or asset to the transferor or gives him a right to reassume power over it (section 98).

Section 97(2) exception: a trust not revocable during the beneficiary's lifetime, or another transfer not revocable during the transferee's lifetime, from which the transferor derives no benefit — clubbing applies only when the power to revoke arises.
concepts.analogy: Giving away income without the asset changes nothing.
concepts.work: Assigning next year's rent to a friend while keeping the flat still taxes the rent in the owner's hands.

concepts.title: Clubbing of spouse and son's wife income
body: Section 99(1)(a)(i): remuneration of a spouse from a concern in which the individual has substantial interest (20% voting power or profit share, alone or with relatives) is clubbed with whichever spouse has the greater income before inclusion, unless it is solely due to the spouse's technical or professional qualification and experience.

Section 99(1)(a)(ii): income from assets transferred to the spouse without adequate consideration (except under an agreement to live apart) is clubbed with the transferor. Section 99(1)(b) applies the same to a son's wife; section 99(1)(d) covers transfers to others for the benefit of spouse or son's wife. Income on the accretion (income from accumulated income) is not clubbed.

Section 99(2): where the asset is invested in a business, the clubbed share is the proportion of the transferred asset's value on the first day of the year to total investment on that day; for investment in a firm as a partner, the interest from the firm is apportioned similarly. House property gifted to a spouse or minor child is instead deemed owned by the transferor under section 25(a).
concepts.analogy: Gifts to spouse or daughter-in-law carry tax back to the giver.
concepts.work: ₹10 lakh gifted to a wife and invested with her own ₹15 lakh clubs 40% of the profit.

concepts.title: Clubbing of minor child's income
body: Section 99(1)(c): all income of a minor child is clubbed with the parent whose income (before inclusion) is greater; if the marriage does not subsist, with the parent maintaining the child. Once included, it stays with that parent unless the AO decides otherwise after a hearing. It applies even to a minor married daughter.

Exceptions: income from manual work by the minor, from activities using the minor's skill, talent or specialised knowledge, and income of a minor suffering from a disability specified in section 154. Such income is taxed in the minor's own hands.
Schedule III (Sl. No. 17) exempts up to ₹1,500 per child of clubbed income — but only if the parent opts out of the default regime.
concepts.analogy: The richer parent pays tax on the child's passive income.
concepts.work: Interest of ₹4,000 on a child's FD is clubbed at ₹2,500 under the optional regime.

concepts.title: HUF conversions, deemed ownership and recovery
body: Section 99(3): where an individual converts his separate property into HUF property or throws it into the common stock, income from it is clubbed with the individual. After a partition, income from the share received by his spouse is also clubbed.

Section 25(a) makes a transferor of house property to a spouse (unless the couple has agreed to live apart) or to a minor child who is not a married daughter the deemed owner, so clubbing provisions and the minor-child exemption do not apply to it.
Section 100: tax on clubbed income may be recovered from the transferee, who is liable for the portion of tax attributable to it; joint holders are jointly and severally liable.
concepts.analogy: Throwing property into the HUF pot does not shift the tax.
concepts.work: A father who converts his flat into HUF property is still taxed on its rent.

jobs.title: Family tax review
jobs.situation: A client has gifted funds to his wife and minor children.
steps: Trace each gifted asset and its income.
Apply the proportion rule for business investments.
Pick the parent with higher income.
Check regime choice for the ₹1,500 exemption.
jobs.takeaway: Gifts within the family need a clubbing check every year.

mcqs.explain: Section 99 does not reach a brother. In practice: the brother pays tax on it.

mcqs.q: Minor child's income from performing in concerts is:
mcqs.explain: Skill-based exception. In practice: file child's return.

options: Opts out of the default regime
mcqs.explain: Schedule III Sl. No. 17. In practice: compare regimes.

mcqs.q: Minor's income where parents are married goes to the parent whose income before inclusion is:
mcqs.explain: Section 99(1)(c). In practice: fixed in later years.

mcqs.explain: Deemed ownership. In practice: not clubbing.

mcqs.explain: Section 99(3). In practice: also after partition for spouse's share.

viva.model: When it provides for re-transfer of the income or asset to the transferor or gives him a right to reassume power over it.

viva.q: Is income from accumulated income of a gifted asset clubbed?
viva.model: It stays with the spouse; only the income from the original asset is clubbed.

viva.q: Which minor's income is taxed in the minor's own hands?
viva.model: Income from manual work, from skill or talent, and income of a minor with a specified disability.

viva.q: Who can be served notice for tax on clubbed income?
viva.model: The transferee, who is liable for the tax attributable to the clubbed income.

viva.q: How is income clubbed when gifted money is invested in a business?
viva.model: In the ratio of the gifted amount to total investment on the first day of the tax year.
